newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares level off after correction.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares level off after correction.

text.p: Russian shares leveled off in afternoon trading on Tuesday after a two-day correction, but the market will remain jittery for the next few days, brokers said.
Prices have found support and the correction seems close to being over, they said.
At 1220 GMT Rostelekom had risen to $3.31 from $3.29 at Monday's close. LUKoil was $14.10 after $14.17, Irkutskenergo was $0.240 after $0.246 and Mosenergo fell to $1.44 from $1.46.

"I expect the market will be stronger in the evening, especially as New York opens, but not much stronger," said ATON trader Boris Shvedsky, adding that Tuesday's buying came both from Russian and Western buyers.

"Every market that is rallying has to have a profit-taking session. All last week everyone was looking for a reason for a correction, and this reason turned out to be Yeltsin's health," said Dan Rapoport, director of institutional equity sales at CentreInvest Securities.

The Kremlin announced on Monday that President Boris Yeltsin was cancelling a visit to the Netherlands on doctors' orders, but dealers said the market was unaffected by news Yeltsin had returned to work at the Kremlin on Tuesday and met Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.
